blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Part I of the Indian Constitution encompasses Articles 1 to 4, dealing with the Union and its Territory.
Article 1 deals with the name and territory of India.
Article 2 provides for the admission or establishment of new states into the Indian Union.
Article 3 empowers Parliament regarding the formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states.
The States Reorganisation Act of 1956 was a landmark legislation in the chronological evolution of Indian states.
INTRODUCTION

blocks.content: The Union and its Territory forms the foundation of the political and geographical structure of India. This chapter explains how India is organized as a Union of States, how new states are formed, how boundaries are altered, and how the Union Territories are administered.

This topic is extremely important for competitive examinations such as UPSC, , State PCS, and other government exams because it involves constitutional provisions, historical evolution, and political structure of India.
PART I OF THE INDIAN CONSTITUTION (ARTICLES 1–4)
Part I of the Indian Constitution deals with the Union and its Territory. It includes Articles 1 to 4, which define:

items:
• The name of the country
  • The territorial extent of India
  • Admission or creation of new states
  • Power of Parliament to reorganize states
The name of the country
The territorial extent of India
Admission or creation of new states
Power of Parliament to reorganize states

blocks.content: These articles give flexibility to the Indian political system.
ARTICLE 1 – NAME AND TERRITORY OF INDIA
“India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.”
It clearly mentions three components of the territory of India:

items: States
Union Territories
Territories that may be acquired in future

• India is described as a 'Union' and not a 'Federation'.
  • This means states have no right to secede.
  • The Indian federation is indestructible.
India is described as a 'Union' and not a 'Federation'.
This means states have no right to secede.

blocks.content: IMPORTANCE OF UNION AND ITS TERRITORY

items:
• Maintains unity and integrity of India
  • Allows flexibility in administration
  • Helps in balanced regional development
  • Ensures strong central authority
  • Prevents secessionist tendencies
Maintains unity and integrity of India

blocks.content: The provisions related to Union and its Territory make India a strong yet flexible federation. The Constitution empowers Parliament to reorganize states as per changing needs while preserving national unity. This balance between unity and diversity is the backbone of Indian federalism.
